title: Ephemeral Geo
imageAlt: Ephemeral Geo glowing route logo and wordmark on a black topographic background
summary: An iPhone app that turns nearby places into time-limited exploration quests.
description:
Ephemeral Geo makes everyday exploration feel like a quest. Choose how far you want to travel and the app finds a nearby destination, gives you a time limit and sets a small observation challenge to complete when you arrive.

Quests can open in Apple Maps, Google Maps or Waze. Arrival can be verified using location, and each completed journey can include a photo or note. The journal keeps a history and map of explored places, while favourites and achievements turn individual trips into a longer exploration record.

The app is being prepared for the App Store. I’ll add the download link here as soon as the listing is live.

title: Football Management Panel
imageAlt: Football Management Panel application interface running beside the Java project workspace
summary: An educational JavaFX desktop application for football managers to organise teams, players and positions.
description:
This was an educational project built around a larger Java codebase. It gives football managers a place to manage their teams, assign players to positions on the field, move players between teams and switch to an available team using manager IDs.

It also gave me experience with exception handling and building a multi-screen desktop interface with JavaFX.

title: FileDrop
imageAlt: FileDrop parachute logo on a sky-blue background
summary: A tool for sharing files between Mac and Windows computers over the same Wi-Fi network.
description:
FileDrop lets you send files directly between Mac and Windows computers on the same Wi-Fi or Ethernet network, without accounts or cloud storage.

Under the hood, the desktop app is built with Tauri. The Angular and TypeScript frontend handles the single-page interface, nearby device list, file selection and transfer progress, while the Rust backend handles local-network discovery and the file transfers themselves. Devices advertise over mDNS, then transfer files directly over a TCP connection. The receiver can accept or deny the request, and Tauri events pass transfer status and progress back to the Angular interface.

The project is still in development. The latest code and progress are on GitHub.

title: REM
imageAlt: REM eye logo glowing above the REM wordmark on a dark navy background
summary: A local-first Windows assistant that sees your screen, calls tools and speaks back, running entirely on local models.
description:
REM is a local-first Windows assistant focused on tool use, system awareness and persistent memory. It runs on local models through Ollama, so nothing has to leave the machine.

The current milestone covers a desktop app shell, a Windows system-info tool, multi-monitor screenshot capture and a vision-model path for screen understanding, plus a first-pass local file tool for reading, writing and browsing files. The first-run goal is simple: start REM, confirm it's online, ask for hardware info, let it call a local tool and answer with the local model, then ask what's on screen and let it use the local vision model to answer.

It's early, but the direction is clear: voice control, spoken responses, visible reasoning, and eventually full smart-home integration, all running locally.
